summary: The narrator, alone in an isolated office, has lost contact with the outside world after Alex Goddard let her make a brief call and then blocked the line. Hoping to find another way out or learn what is going on, she tries keys from a ring on the desk and unlocks a steel door, revealing a fully equipped medical research lab. Among the equipment is a bronze Dancing Shiva statue on the workbench, and the passage ends with noises and heavy boots approaching in the hall.
one_line: Isolated in an office, the narrator unlocks a steel door to find a medical research lab with a bronze Dancing Shiva, as footsteps approach.
key_facts: The narrator had just lost contact with the outside world after Alex Goddard let her tell a couple of people she was physically okay, then blocked the line.
Calvin lives next to the Kiasma museum, as the narrator notes.
The narrator thinks David ignored her distress signal because he was so excited.
A steel door on the left of the office was locked tight.
A ring of keys lay on the desk, and the fifth key tried opened the steel door.
The narrator stopped breathing when footsteps marched up to the door outside but they moved on.
The room behind the door was a fully equipped medical research lab with lights off and several CRT screens above a long lab bench.
The lab contained a large machine, probably a gas chromatograph, with its own screen, flanked by rows of test tubes.
A large electronic microscope with a video screen was in the lab.
A two-foot-high bronze Dancing Shiva stood in the middle of the workbench.
The narrator describes the Dancing Shiva statue as breath-takingly beautiful and calls it The Lord of the Dance.
Clanking noises and the pounding of heavy boots were heard in the hall as the passage ends.
